classification.difficultyReason: Plot each absolute-value function with its horizontal comparison line, translate intersections into solution x-values, and interpret no intersection and a single vertex intersection. Part a explicitly models the graphical procedure used in part b.

content.prompt: [Technology] Use suitable graphing software to help solve these problems.

children.label: i
children.prompt: Sketch $y=|x-4|$ and $y=1$ on the same set of axes, clearly showing the points of intersection.

answer.worked: Plot the V with vertex $(4,0)$ and y-intercept 4. The horizontal line $y=1$ crosses its branches at $(3,1)$ and $(5,1)$.

spec.description: V and comparison line on common axes, with intersection guides and coordinates. House blue distinguishes the comparison function.

children.label: ii
children.prompt: Hence write down the solution of $|x-4|=1$.

answer.worked: The x-coordinates of the two intersection points are 3 and 5, so $x=3$ or $x=5$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Now use similar graphical methods to solve each of the following.

answer.worked: Plot $y=|x+3|$ and $y=1$. The line intersects the V at $(-4,1)$ and $(-2,1)$, so $x=-4$ or $x=-2$.

spec.description: Comparison line y=1, vertex -3, intersection guides at -4 and -2, y-intercept 3.

answer.worked: Plot $y=|2x+1|$ and $y=3$. The line intersects the V at $(-2,3)$ and $(1,3)$, so $x=-2$ or $x=1$.

spec.description: Vertex (-1/2,0), y-intercept 1, comparison line y=3 and guides at x=-2,1.

answer.worked: Plot $y=|3x-3|$ and $y=-2$. The V lies on or above the x-axis, while the horizontal line lies below it. The graphs have no intersection, so there is no solution.

spec.description: V with vertex (1,0), y-intercept 3 and separate line y=-2.

answer.worked: Plot $y=|2x-5|$ and $y=0$, the x-axis. They meet only at the vertex $(\frac52,0)$, so $x=\frac52$.

spec.description: The x-axis supplies y=0. The V meets it once at x=5/2, with y-intercept 5.
